reason: Checked against the source. Callers: every JSR sfx_write / sfx_write.ddra_set_c046b / BRA into it (sfx_output tone low/high, amplitude, .noise, sfx_next_ramp.ended via sfx_tick's two JSR sfx_next_ramp and sfx_silence) reloads A or ignores A and Z/N after (LDA sfx_p_hi, LDA sfx_v, LDA sfx_dp, DEX/BPL, PLP); sfx_silence's two callers in bank5.6502 (LDA #&FF; and CLI then JMP clear_title_screen, which starts LDA #&13) and sfx_tick's caller in irq1_handler (PLA STA romsel, PLA PLY PLX RTI) never read A, Y or flags. Y is 0 on return either way (wait_low exits at 0; sfx_silence's comment holds), X untouched, the ORB byte &08 is the same value from A instead of Y. Not PROTECTED, not a generated source (sfx_data.6502 and compiled_bank5.6502 only move 5 bytes down, unedited; labels, no alignment ASSERT on them; bank 5 shrinks, so Room is fine). No ROMSEL/ANDY/ACCCON-X issue: the code touches only the System VIA and bank 5's own tables, as before. Not raster-timed: sfx_tick runs last in the vsync handler, after the palette write, User VIA T1 split setup and the flip, so a shorter tick only returns sooner. Sound: the same bytes in the same order to the chip; write enable is still held low for wait_low's 17 cycles (8.5us > the SN76489's 32 clocks at 4MHz), and after the rise the next data-bus change is tens of cycles later on every path (next sfx_write, or the main program's keyboard read only after RTI; sfx_silence's CLI path is RTS+DEX+BPL+PLP+RTS+CLI+interrupt entry first); the post-rise wait is the MOS's margin, not a chip requirement (common BBC SN76489 write idiom). Cycles: LDY #4 (2) + 4 DEY (8) + 3 taken BNE (9) + 1 untaken (2) = 21; bytes 2+1+2 = 5. Residual: real-hardware sound timing is not something jsbeeb can prove; worth a hardware listen with the rest of the round.
